A skill is a saved set of instructions Claude runs when you type `/` and its
name (see the [Thesaurus](thesaurus.qmd#foundations)). Each one below lives in
the `.claude/skills/` folder of its session, is plain English, and can be
copied into any project of yours. Download a session to get the files, or read
them on [GitHub](https://github.com/nelsonamayad-jf/from-asking-to-doing).

Two conventions run through all of them:

- **Defaults live in `CLAUDE.md`, not in the skill.** Colours, fonts, page
  limits, output folders: change them in the session's `CLAUDE.md` and every
  skill picks them up.
- **Nothing final is written without a pause.** Each session has a review gate
  where the skill shows you its plan and waits.

## Session 1 · Slidemaking {#session-1}

::: {.catalog-entry}
### `/proposal-to-slides`

::: {.catalog-meta}
[Session 1](01_slidemaker/session-1.qmd) · input: a proposal (`.md`, `.txt`, `.docx`) · output: `output/*.pptx` · needs Node.js, LibreOffice, Poppler, Pandoc
:::

Reads a proposal document and turns it into an on-brand deck. It takes the
template path, colours, fonts and slide rules from `CLAUDE.md`, renders the
`.potx` template to images to copy its look, proposes a slide plan and waits for
confirmation, then builds the file with `pptxgenjs` and checks every page. A
supporting reference, `skills/pptx/SKILL.md`, holds the mechanics of building
and QA-ing a `.pptx`; it is not a command you run.

```text
/proposal-to-slides input/research-proposal.md
```
:::

## Session 2 · Mixing it up {#session-2}

Three skills that hand files to each other, plus one that runs them all.

::: {.catalog-entry}
### `/collect`

::: {.catalog-meta}
[Session 2](02_summarizer/session-2.qmd) · input: a folder (default `sample-inputs/`) · output: `output/manifest.md`
:::

Scans the input folder, classifies every file by type and likely content, and
writes a manifest. This is the step to re-run when you add a file.

```text
/collect
/collect path/to/your/folder
```
:::

::: {.catalog-entry}
### `/synthesize`

::: {.catalog-meta}
[Session 2](02_summarizer/session-2.qmd) · input: `output/manifest.md` and the files it lists · output: `output/summaries/`
:::

Reads each file in the manifest and writes a structured summary per input.
Inside this step the work is delegated to agents, one per file type, running in
parallel; that is where Session 2 introduces agents.

```text
/synthesize
```
:::

::: {.catalog-entry}
### `/report`

::: {.catalog-meta}
[Session 2](02_summarizer/session-2.qmd) · input: `output/summaries/` · output: `output/summary-report.docx` · needs Python (`python-docx`)
:::

Assembles the summaries into one Word report using the defaults in
`CLAUDE.md` (ten pages at most, numbered headings, English). Before writing it
prints the proposed structure and asks whether to add, remove or rename
sections. That pause is the review gate.

```text
/report
```
:::

::: {.catalog-entry .orchestrator}
### `/summarizer`

::: {.catalog-meta}
[Session 2](02_summarizer/session-2.qmd) · runs `/collect` → `/synthesize` → `/report` · optional folder argument
:::

The orchestrator: all three steps in sequence, still stopping at the report
gate. Good for the demo; the step-by-step version is better for learning,
because you can inspect each intermediate file.

```text
/summarizer
/summarizer path/to/your/folder
```
:::

## Session 3 · Extended Team {#session-3}

Two agent skills with deliberately separate inputs, plus the orchestrator that
runs them in order.

::: {.catalog-entry .agent}
### `/researcher`

::: {.catalog-meta}
[Session 3](03_multitudes/session-3.qmd) · input: `sample-input/` (the strategy, the prior strategy, org context) · output: `output/research-briefing.md`
:::

Reads the strategy and every context file and builds an evidence briefing:
what the document claims, what the other files say, where they agree and
conflict. It forms no opinion. The briefing is where the human checkpoint sits:
fix the evidence here before anything judges it.

```text
/researcher
```
:::

::: {.catalog-entry .agent}
### `/reviewer`

::: {.catalog-meta}
[Session 3](03_multitudes/session-3.qmd) · input: `output/research-briefing.md` only · output: `output/review-findings.md`
:::

Applies a five-lens critique framework to the briefing and produces ranked
findings with confidence ratings. It never reads the original strategy, which
is what stops it from rationalising evidence toward a conclusion. Every
finding cites a source file and passage; untraceable claims are dropped.

```text
/reviewer
```
:::

::: {.catalog-entry .orchestrator}
### `/strategy-review`

::: {.catalog-meta}
[Session 3](03_multitudes/session-3.qmd) · runs `/researcher` → checkpoint → `/reviewer` → report · output: `output/strategy-review-report.docx`, `output/audit-log.md` · needs Python (`python-docx`)
:::

Runs both agents in order, stops at the checkpoint between them, and then
formats the findings into a Word report for decision-makers. It also writes the
audit log: every action taken, every source cited, every decision made.

```text
/strategy-review
```
:::

## Making your own

Copy the closest one. A skill is a `SKILL.md` file in `.claude/skills/<name>/`
with a short front matter (`name`, `description`) and the procedure in plain
English. Sessions 2 and 3 keep the procedure in a readable `skills/<name>.md`
and have the `SKILL.md` point to it; Session 1 keeps the whole procedure in the
`SKILL.md`. Either works. The official reference is
[Skills in the Claude Code docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills).
